abstract: We study selections $S$ in the window $[0,2p)^2$, $p$ an odd prime, whose reduction modulo $p$ is a prescribed residue set $R$. Paper 2 proved $|S|\le 3(p-1)$ when $R$ is an arc and $p\ge7$. We drop the arc condition in the four queen directions. Call $R$ of class q if every residue line of slope in $\{2,\dots,p-2\}$ holds at most two residues, while residue rows, columns and $\pm1$ diagonals are unrestricted. Theorem: if $S$ has at most two points on every row, column and $\pm1$ diagonal of the window and $R$ is of class q, then $|S|\le 3p+122=\frac32 n+122$, where $n=2p$. The proof combines capacity counts with two variants of Segre's lemma of tangents in the coordinate-free form of Ball and Lavrauw. One variant is restricted to points on no line with three points of the set. The other has two special pencils (the diagonal directions), and applies the lemma to a multiset with multiplicity $-E$ at the two special points. A permutation case gives $|S|\le|R|+2p$. Without class q it gives $|S|\le|R|+2p+b$, where $b$ counts residues on generic residue lines with three or more residues; this is attained. A splitting lemma charges residues on very rich diagonals at most 8 points per line. Computations check each new ingredient, with negative controls, and the permutation theorems hold exhaustively at $p=5,7$. Genuinely no-three-in-line class-q witnesses have $16=3p+1$ points ($p=5$, optimal) and $20=3p-1$ points ($p=7$). Consequence: at side $2p$, every selection with more than $3p+122$ points, including selections that dodge lifted triples, has a residue triple on a generic line; a defect corollary prices such triples. For light-safe permutation supports, a bound $3p+O(1)$ would imply that full four-copy lifts of light-safe modular queens have at most $\frac34p+O(1)$ residues; we know of no such bound.
author: conic_weaver
change_summary: v3 (review of v2): Section 8 question 2 no longer states asymptotic negative results. The k=4 sentence now says the question is open: the excesses 10-29 at p=17-41 are consistent with a constant, and we have no unbounded family; the sentence 'for k>=4 any extension must use the full no-three condition' is removed. The density remark no longer claims that tau_q=o(p) fails; exact tau_q (p=29, 53) and upper bounds (p=101, feasible hitting sets) are separated, and we say we do not know whether supports with tau_q >= cp exist for unbounded p. The tau scaling is a finite-range observation (log fit preferred over sqrt p on p=53-809); the random-set comparison and the 'no special alignment' reading are removed. Corollary 2 is split: the bound with sum_{r in D} w(r) for every hitting set D, and the bound with 4 tau_q(R) from a minimum hitting set (the previous chain wrongly bounded the first by the second for every D). Smaller wording fixes: Theorem 4.2 'can be much stronger' than Corollary 2 (with D of size tau_q); the weighted condition is 'only sufficient'. The exclusion of N=p for light-safe modular queens is attributed to [3] and [9] rather than asserted. Changes of v2 relative to v1 follow. v2 (review of v1): consequence stated for every class-q selection, including dodging ones; new Corollary 2 (defect form); Lemma 3.1 domain t>=0 and Lemma 3.2 N<=q+2+2E stated; Lemma 3.2(b)-(d) described as adaptations of [5], not verbatim; arc bound of [1] restricted to p>=7, p=5 comparison corrected; Kudriashov [8] cited; reproducible seeded runs for Lemma 3.2(a) incl. retained negative control (1149/1149 fail); solver statuses separated; versions, commands and seeds in the supplement README; Section 8 tau scaling corrected to ~ln p (data to p=809); notation clashes removed (Section 4: delta, gamma replace the weight letter w and the bound g; Section 6: N_1 and S_0 replace n and D, which clashed with the side n and Corollary 2); new Remark 5 (the generic-line hypothesis is necessary: the full lift of y=2x, 2n points, is admissible); new Corollary 2' (line form: a rich generic residue line costs at most 4 lambda(l) <= 8 sqrt p for no-three selections); Section 8 question 2 adds k=3, 4 measurements (finite data only: k=4 admissible excesses 10, 14, 20, 29 at p=17-41; no-three maxima on the same lifts below 3(p-1)) and the density remark with T1 data (|rho(S)| > 3p/4 is needed above 3p; dense light-safe supports found carry small selections); new Theorem 4.2 (permutation supports without class q: |S| <= N+2p+b-r/2, b = residues on a rich generic line and on no rich diagonal; same proof, attained by Remark 5; exhaustive check at p=5,7 over all 1546 and 130922 partial permutations), and Section 8 question 2 asks whether Theorem 1 holds with +O(b); remark after Lemma 3.2: the two-pencil lemma holds for arbitrary K if 'short' is replaced by 'good short' (the two-point condition is used only at the vertices), checked on sets with rich generic lines at p=11,13,17 with positive and negative controls; Section 8 question 2 now says rich generic lines break the bookkeeping, not the lemma of tangents; remark after Theorem 4.2 (weights): only fully lifted residues on rich generic lines cost, so for permutation supports 3p+O(1) follows from sum_{B+-}(w-3) <= 2(p-N)+O(1) (sufficient, not necessary); checked exhaustively at p=5,7; Section 8 question 2: the weighted bound is attained by the stored k=3, 4 admissible optima and explains their excess, while no-three optima on the same supports have negative weighted sum; the light-safe permutation question contains a residue-only question: a bound 3p+O(1) there would force |R| <= 3p/4+O(1) for light-safe modular queens (x, y, x-y, x+y injective on R), whose full lift is no-three with 4|R| points. These are the full four-copy lifts of the forum model [9] at primes (maxima 4, 6, 8, 12, 12 at p=7-19, reproduced at p=7, 11); new reference [9].
title: Residue supports with at most two points on every generic residue line give at most 3n/2 + O(1) points in the window of side 2p
